coverage.evidence: Quick Add's messages say what happened and what to do next, and this change leaves their wording untouched while making one of them more reliably the only thing shown. A rejected save returns its own message and keeps every value for a retry — 'keeps every value when the write is rejected' passes — and the validation message is rendered in a p with role=alert (quick-add.tsx:272), so it is announced rather than only seen.

No information rests on colour alone on either screen. Quick Add's movement types are radios with visible text labels, not coloured swatches; its validation state is carried by a role=alert message in words, not by a red border alone. Plan's over-allocated state sets overAllocated from free < 0 and the header states it in words beside the figure. Unchanged by this item, which adds no colour and no indicator.

Every control on Quick Add has an accessible name, supplied explicitly rather than inferred: label props at quick-add.tsx:127 Amount, 138 What kind of movement, 154 Movement type, 171 Category, 189 Who this is with, 205 Where it is kept, 219 Date, 233 Note. The sheet itself is a Radix Dialog with a Dialog.Title. Plan's rows are a table with header cells. This change adds no control and renames none.

Every field has a label, through the shared Field and control primitives rather than a placeholder standing in for one: each call site passes label, and the primitives render a real label element wrapping or bound to the input (controls.tsx:19, field.tsx). The eight Quick Add tests reach their fields with getByLabelText, which would fail if any label were missing or not associated.

The whole flow works from the keyboard, and the change touches it in the one place worth checking. The sheet is a Radix Dialog, which traps focus, closes on Escape and restores focus on close. The amount field carries autoFocus (quick-add.tsx:130), so the first thing a keyboard or screen-reader user meets is the field they need. A remount could plausibly have broken that, and demonstrably does not: quick-add.test.tsx:156 asserts document.activeElement is the amount field after opening, and it passes on this commit. Plan's rows are reached by tab and its row menu is a Radix menu.

Focus stays visible. Where the browser outline is suppressed it is replaced: field.tsx:11 sets focus:outline-none together with focus:border-emerald and a 3px focus:ring-em2, which computes to 8.03:1 light and 8.79:1 dark against the card — well past the 3:1 a focus indicator needs. The one other outline-none in the app, onboarding.tsx:184, sits on an h1 with tabIndex -1: it is focused programmatically to announce a step and is never reachable by tab, so suppressing a ring there is correct rather than a gap. Checked rather than assumed.

coverage.reason: No dragging exists on either screen, and none is added. Quick Add's inputs are fields, radios and disclosure tiles; Plan's rows are edited through a form, not by dragging.

coverage.evidence: Computed from the tokens rather than deferred for want of a browser, since contrast is arithmetic on the declared values in apps/web/src/design/tokens.css. Text, WCAG AA 4.5:1: light ink on bg 15.85, ink on card 17.55, soft on bg 5.75, soft on card 6.37, emerald on bg 7.25, emerald on card 8.03; dark ink on bg 16.80, ink on card 15.54, soft on bg 7.51, soft on card 6.95, emerald on bg 9.50, emerald on card 8.79. All twelve pass, worst light soft-on-bg at 5.75:1. The field's focus ring, a user interface component at 3:1, is emerald on card: 8.03 light, 8.79 dark. Nothing in this change alters a token or a colour, so these hold before and after it.

Text follows the person's size setting: every size on both screens comes from the type scale as a token class — text-body, text-small, text-title, text-lab — and no changed line sets a font size, a line height or a fixed text dimension. The one new value in this change is an integer counter that is never rendered.

Touch targets meet the minimum, and it is a token rather than a habit: --target-min is 44px (tokens.css:92), exposed as min-h-target and min-w-target, and every interactive primitive these screens use applies it — button.tsx:9, controls.tsx:19, :123, :182, field.tsx:5. There is also a --target-gap of 8px for spacing between them. No target is added or resized by this change.

Animation respects the setting, and it is handled centrally rather than per component: tokens.css:173 carries an @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block, and docs/design/motion.md:121 states the preference is mandatory with an entry for every motion in its section 3. The durations these screens use are tokens that block governs. This change adds no animation; it does change when the sheet's contents mount, which is a mount rather than a transition and carries no motion of its own.

summary: Pass, nothing open. The rule worth checking was DES-10: a remount could have broken focus on open, and it demonstrably does not — the amount field still holds focus, asserted by a test that reads document.activeElement. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred: all twelve text pairs clear 4.5:1, worst 5.75:1, and the focus ring clears 3:1 at 8:1. Targets are a 44px token, reduced motion is handled centrally.
